title: Localization preserves finite ring maps
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and let $S\subseteq A$ be a multiplicative submonoid, meaning $1\in S$ and $s,t\in S$ implies $st\in S$. Write $S^{-1}A$ for the ring of fractions $a/s$, where $a/s=a'/s'$ if and only if $v(as'-a' s)=0$ for some $v\in S$, with addition and multiplication $(a/s)+(a'/s')=(as'+a' s)/(ss')$ and $(a/s)(a'/s')=aa'/(ss')$. Write $S^{-1}B$ for the same construction in $B$ using the submonoid $\varphi(S)$. Then the induced homomorphism $S^{-1}A\to S^{-1}B$, $a/s\mapsto\varphi(a)/\varphi(s)$, is finite (the localized target is a finitely generated module over the localized base).
